subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: Data handling & access controls
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@fintrust.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Data handling & access controls — summary + next steps

Hi Rajiv / Anika,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap from our side on the data handling and access-control topics you asked about, plus proposed next steps: 

Summary:
- PII classification: Redwood treats user identifiers and profile PII as sensitive by default. We support column-level encryption at rest and field-masking at inference time for token filtering.
- Data retention: Hosted API customers can set retention windows (30 / 90 / 365 days) and we support custom retention policies for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Logging & auditing: Request-level logs are available with token granularity in the Console; audit trails for config changes and user actions are retained per your retention policy and can be exported to your logging stack (S3/BigQuery).
- Access controls & support access: RBAC with role templates (admin, dev, auditor, support-readonly). Support access is gated via Just-In-Time (JIT) break-glass requests that require an approved ticket and generate an immutable audit record; customer opt-in is required for elevated break-glass sessions.

Attachments I’m including: SOC2-Summary.pdf (high-level attestation) and a short access-control matrix (redwood-access-controls-matrix.xlsx) showing roles, privileges, and support escalation workflow.

Proposed next steps:
1) Share the access-control matrix with your security team — I’ve attached it.
2) If you’d like, Dylan can join a short call to walk through RBAC, break-glass flows, and sample audit logs.
3) Please confirm the minimum retention window you require and whether you need data residency in us-east or a dedicated VPC.

Can you let me know by EOD Monday which of the above you want to prioritize? Happy to schedule the follow-up.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@fintrust.io>

Cc: Anika Shah <anika.shah@fintrust.io>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Data handling & access controls — summary + next steps

Thanks Marissa — that recap is helpful. Quick clarifying points from our security team: 

1) PII: We need confirmation that Redwood can redact or prevent retention of PII at the field level before writing to any persistent store in the hosted flow (not just mask in UI). Is there an API-level hook or pre-ingest filter?

2) Break-glass: Our policy requires break-glass sessions to be time-limited to 1 hour and require both a ticket and 2 approvers from our security team. Can Redwood accommodate that workflow, or do we have to adopt Redwood's standard process?

3) Audit logs: We need export to our SIEM (Splunk) in near-real-time (under 5 minutes). Is streaming of request logs supported?

We’d like Dylan to join the follow-up call — can you do the walkthrough next week? Also, please confirm whether data residency in AWS us-east-1 is supported for hosted accounts (we prefer region-specific isolation).

Thanks,
Rajiv
Head of InfoSec | FinTrust
rajiv@fintrust.io

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Data handling & access controls — summary + next steps

Rajiv — great questions, and all addressable. Short answers below and proposed technical owners for the call: 

1) PII pre-ingest filtering: Yes — Redwood provides request-side pre-processing hooks for Hosted customers via a configured pre-ingest filter chain. That lets you redact/transform fields before any persistence. For Dedicated/Private we can install the filter as a customer-controlled module. (Owner: Dylan Brooks)

2) Break-glass workflow: We support configurable timeouts and multi-approver workflows for break-glass. Our standard flow is 2 approvers for critical sessions and default timeout is 30 minutes, but we can extend to 1 hour and require 2 customer approvers as you described. Break-glass sessions generate immutable audit events and are logged to the audit index. (Owner: Monica Patel — she'll share the flow docs)

3) Audit log streaming: We support near-real-time streaming of audit and request logs to customer endpoints (S3, Splunk HTTP Event Collector, BigQuery). Typical latency is under 2 minutes. We’ll include a sample Splunk HEC config in the follow-up doc.

Next steps:
- Dylan / Monica to join a 30-min technical deep-dive next Tue (Aug 25) at 10:00 AM PT — are you available?
- I’ll share a short JIT break-glass runbook and the Splunk HEC sample config ahead of the call.
- If you need, I can also request a short Dedicated/Private sizing sketch for your security requirements.

If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
